atoms.title: At the Palm and Pepper in Chicago

atoms.sound: After a long day at work, Hannah and Eisa sat down at their usual table, ready to order and unwind. Hannah had something on her mind.<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3Us_chirp'>“Listen. What’s happening with Ice is horrible. But wouldn’t you agree immigration can be complicated? I mean, you speak English well, you work here, you’re a good citizen, but…”</voice>Eisa cut her off. <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f5Us_chirp'>“Well, when my parents fled Chile, they were escaping a brutal government. They didn’t have the luxury of learning English. They had to survive. Their English is broken, so what? They work, pay taxes, take care of their neighborhood. Integration isn’t a one-way street where we sand down who we are until we’re acceptable. It goes both ways. The U.S. changes too. And maybe that’s what scares people.”</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3Us_chirp'>“You’re right. Technically, my ancestors were immigrants too. They were English settlers that came here in the eighteenth century, though their story isn’t exactly a noble one, settling on indigenous lands. My Jewish ancestors however, came from Russia through Ellis Island in the nineteenth century. They must have had it hard, like yours.”</voice>

atoms.a:
What is Isa's migration background?
(2 correct answers)

What is Hannah's migration background?
(3 correct answers)

Why did Isa's parents immigrate to the US?
(1 correct answer)
b: They wanted to escape from paying taxes.
++They escaped from the dictatorship in Chile.

atoms.a:
Where did Hannah's ancestors arrive?
(2 correct answers)

What are their opinions on immigration?
(2 correct answers)
b: ++Hannah thinks that immigration can have issues.
Hannah is against immigration, and believes people should speak English well.
++Isa believes that integration means change for both the immigrant and the country they migrate to.
Isa thinks that it's unnecessary to learn a new language.

atoms.sound: Back in the kitchen, sue chef Ying Yue kept the restaurant running with precision. She had grown up in her parents' small Chinese restaurant in San Francisco; a photo of her and her mother cooking, was taped inside her locker. Sadly, she barely spoke Chinese because her parents had mostly spoken English at home. While her dad had immigrated from Taiwan to the US in the 90s, her family’s roots in the United States ran deep. Her mother’s ancestors had arrived generations ago from China to build the railroads. A copy of an old work certificate hung beside the family photo, proof that their labor had helped build the nation and her life.

atoms.a:
What is Ying Yue's migration background?
(2 correct answers)

When did her ancestors immigrate?
(2 correct answers)
b: ++Her mother's ancestors arrived as workers in the 1840s.
Her mother's ancestors arrived as traders in the 1740s.

atoms.a:
What objects does Ying Yue have in her locker?
(1 correct answer)
b: A rental contract and a small painting.
++A labour contract and a family photo.
A keychain and a family painting.

instruction.text: Listen carefully, then answer the questions.

atoms.sound: Meanwhile, Ife, the restaurant’s owner, prepared his signature Jamaican curry. He put in all his passion into the dish. Confident that the kitchen was running smoothly, he left and took the curry upstairs to his neighbor, Ximena. In recent weeks, ICE raids had left her too frightened to leave her flat. Undocumented her entire life, she had come from Mexico and worked for decades as a cleaner; essential, invisible, and unprotected. Now she lived in constant uncertainty.When she opened the door, her face lit up. <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f4Us_chirp'>“Ayy, Efe, you don’t have to do this.”</voice> she said, though he knew she was happy he came. He thought of his mother, who had fought to immigrate from Jamaica and worked tirelessly once she arrived. Ximena’s story echoed hers: the same determination to survive, to provide, to carve out dignity in a country that offered opportunity with one hand and exclusion with the other. On his father’s side, the story was harsher still. His ancestors were forced into slavery, their suffering woven into the nation’s foundations. The debt of that history lingered in the racism Ife still faced so often. And yet, this was his country. He would not stand by but instead support Ximena.As they sat down to eat, Ximena’s granddaughter Maria arrived as she did every evening to bring groceries. Born in the United States and a citizen, Maria was finishing her PhD in mechanical engineering, an achievement built on her grandmother’s and parents’ sacrifices. She joined them at the small table. Together they shared a meal and brought a little light into a dark time by celebrating community in their very small way.

atoms.a:
What is Ximena's migration background?
(1 correct answer)

What is Ife's migration background?
(2 correct answers)

Why does Ife bring Ximena his curry?
(2 correct answers)
b: She has difficulty walking because of her age.
Her grandchild Maria is visiting and he wants to surprise them.
++She cannot leave the house because ICE could detain her in public.
He always cooks food for his neighbours.
++He believes she is a valuable part of society like his mother and other immigrants no matter her legal status.

atoms.a:
Where are the parallels between Ife and Maria?
(3 correct answers)
b: Their families have the same migration background.
++Ife and Maria are both citizen of the US.
++They both support Ximena with food supplies and company.
++Their families have worked hard so they would be able to have a successful live.
They both believe that Ximena should return to Mexico.
